newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Network computing drives IBM's Asia growth.
newsitem.headline: Network computing drives IBM's Asia growth.

text.p: Network computing is driving IBM Singapore's growth in Asia, managing director Lawrence Wee said on Wednesday.
Wee told a news conference that countries like Singapore, Taiwan and Japan were at the forefront in connecting their businesses to corporate networks as well as to the Internet.
Other Asian countries like Malaysia, South Korea and Hong Kong showed strong demand potential for hardware, software and services needed to connect to networks, he said.
There were "pockets of interest" from specific customers and institutions for network computing products and services from countries like Indonesia, Philippines and China, he added.

IBM's revenue from ASEAN (the Association of Southeast Asian Nations) was expected to grow more than 30 percent in 1996, after rising more than 20 percent in 1995, said KB Low, director of market management for IBM ASEAN and South Asia.
ASEAN contributed slightly more than 1.0 percent to IBM's total worldwide revenue, Low said. ASEAN comprises Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia, Philippines, Brunei and Vietnam.
IBM reported worldwide revenue of US$52.8 billion for the first nine months in 1996.
Wee said riding on the network computing wave, IBM Singapore's revenue should grow faster than the information technology industry growth rate in Singapore.

Singapore's National Computer Board said on Tuesday the city-state's information technology revenue had risen 34.3 percent in 1995 to a record S$6.7 billion and that it expected the industry to grow more than 30 percent in 1996.
"If that is in fact the number that they have published, we can organise ourselves to make sure we do that (grow faster)," said Wee.
